authority_precedence.description: Versioned machine-readable or explicitly normative record on the protected branch.
Digest-bound workflow, release, certificate, or artifact evidence for an exact subject.
Exact-subject review or decision whose jurisdiction is defined by protected policy.
Reconstructible view generated from protected records and evidence.
Navigation, discussion, and operational coordination surface only.

record_classes.title: Campaign lifecycle manifest
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected Programme records define lifecycle and route state.
record_classes.historical_rule: Historical manifests are immutable and marked superseded or terminal.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Successors identify the prior record and preserve claim and route lineage.

record_classes.title: Provider provenance manifest
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected Forge records define source identity and provenance.
record_classes.historical_rule: Prior source revisions remain immutable and non-current.
record_classes.supersession_rule: New revisions identify predecessors and trigger consumer review.

record_classes.title: Solve work-package manifest
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected Solve records define producer state and bounded scope.
record_classes.historical_rule: Completed and superseded work packages remain immutable.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Successors preserve lineage, blockers, and evidence.

record_classes.title: Certification route and adjudication
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected Cert records define certification state and scope.
record_classes.historical_rule: Prior adjudications and outputs remain immutable.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Re-adjudication identifies the prior route, subject, and evidence.

record_classes.title: Solve-to-Cert handoff
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected handoffs define submission readiness, not adjudication.
record_classes.historical_rule: Consumed and superseded handoffs remain immutable.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Corrections identify prior packets and material changes.

record_classes.title: Programme claim ledger
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected Programme ledgers control claim status; local records may narrow only.
record_classes.historical_rule: Earlier claim states remain immutable with their evidence.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Changes identify predecessor state and changed evidence.

record_classes.title: Review and decision record
record_classes.current_state_rule: A review is valid only for its exact subject and jurisdiction.
record_classes.historical_rule: Reviews remain immutable; stale reviews cannot authorize changed subjects.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Later reviews identify corrected or replaced records.

record_classes.title: Promotion and closure record
record_classes.current_state_rule: Promotion is effective only through a protected record after named gates pass.
record_classes.historical_rule: Prior promotion, rejection, and closure records remain immutable.
record_classes.supersession_rule: New dispositions preserve prior subject and decision identities.

record_classes.title: Waiver and emergency record
record_classes.current_state_rule: Only unexpired protected waivers apply within approved scope.
record_classes.historical_rule: Expired, revoked, and superseded waivers remain immutable.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Renewal identifies the prior waiver and preserves prohibited uses.

record_classes.title: Evidence and artifact manifest
record_classes.current_state_rule: Evidence is valid only for its exact subject, producer, bytes, and expiry.
record_classes.historical_rule: Expired evidence remains auditable but cannot satisfy current gates by default.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Replacement evidence preserves prior identity and explains insufficiency.

record_classes.title: Negative-knowledge record
record_classes.current_state_rule: Protected records control exclusions only within exact assumptions and scope.
record_classes.historical_rule: Negative results remain immutable after reopening or supersession.
record_classes.supersession_rule: Reopening identifies the prior record, changed premise, and trigger.
